# GeoTag Camera

> Free, open source (GPL-3.0-or-later), ad-free Android camera app that stamps photos with GPS location, address and time, and signs each photo on the device so anyone can later check it hasn't been edited. Built by Konko Maji for field surveyors, inspectors, students and NGO teams. Capturing, stamping, signing and verifying work offline. No Google Play services, no ads, no analytics, no trackers, no account.

## Key facts

- Current version: {{version}}, the first full (non-preview) release
- Platform: Android 8.0 (API 26) and newer; Kotlin, CameraX, Jetpack Compose
- Package name: com.geotagcamera.geotagginglocationonphoto
- License: GNU GPL v3.0 or later
- Price: free; no ads, subscriptions or in-app purchases
- Data collection: none; there is no developer server, no analytics SDK, no ad SDK, no crash reporter, no account
- Google Play services: not needed; location comes from Android's own location services
- Permissions: camera; location (only while the camera screen is visible); photo location (so Verify can read GPS data in a picked photo); storage only on Android 9 and older; internet only for the stamp map, offline map downloads and the optional weather chip
- Downloads: signed APKs on GitHub releases, one per CPU type (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64) plus universal, each with a .sha256 file
- Stores: GitHub releases now (the only official download today); F-Droid (submission in review, reproducible builds, same signature as GitHub) and Google Play coming soon. Not published anywhere else.
- Upgrading from 1.3.0 or older: uninstall first (new permanent signing key); photos stay in the gallery and still verify; Gallery, Import photos re-adds them to the in-app list
- Author: Konko Maji (konkomaji@gmail.com)

## Features ({{version}})

- Live stamp preview in the viewfinder, drawn by the same code that burns the stamp into the photo
- Compact Bar stamp (place and country, address with Plus Code, coordinates, date and time with GMT offset, accuracy/altitude/bearing/weather, map, organisation name, logo and signature; about a sixth of a portrait photo) or a small Minimal label; moved by long-press and drag
- GPS position, altitude, accuracy, direction, time and time-zone offset also written to EXIF
- On-device OpenStreetMap map on the stamp (MapLibre + OpenFreeMap, no API key); cached for offline use; whole 2-30 km areas can be saved before a trip
- Field and Professional profiles chosen at first launch
- Projects: shoot into a project, filter the gallery, move photos between projects
- Sticky note and a fixed custom text line on the stamp
- Export locations as CSV, KML or GeoJSON with each photo's SHA-256
- PDF site report with an overview map, an index and a fresh verification of each photo
- Import photos: re-adds GeoTag Camera photos from the phone's gallery to the in-app list
- Verify any photo carrying a GeoTag Camera proof, including ones from other people, offline
- Camera adapts to the phone: real lens zoom presets, flash only if present, maker Night/HDR/Portrait modes via CameraX Extensions, 4:3/16:9/1:1/Full
- In-app privacy policy, terms and licences; Report a problem by email (nothing sent automatically)

## How verification works

At capture the app hashes the JPEG image data (metadata segments excluded) with SHA-256 and signs the hash together with the capture latitude, longitude and time using an ECDSA P-256 key generated in the Android Keystore. Hash, signature and public key are embedded in EXIF and XMP. Verification recomputes the hash, checks the signature against the embedded key and compares the EXIF latitude, longitude and time with the signed values. A pass means the pixels (including the stamp) and the signed location and time are unchanged since signing. It does not prove who took the photo (the key is not tied to a person; compare the key fingerprint), nor that the GPS or clock were accurate. Recompressing a photo breaks verification.

## What leaves the phone

Nothing goes to the developer. The stamp map downloads OpenStreetMap tiles from OpenFreeMap (tile coordinates and IP address). The optional weather chip (off by default) sends the position rounded to about 1 km to Open-Meteo. Address lookup uses the phone's built-in Android geocoder, which on phones with Google services is usually Google's. App data is excluded from cloud backup and device transfer.

## Common questions

- What is GeoTag Camera? A free, open-source Android camera that stamps GPS location, address, a map and the time onto photos and signs each photo so later edits can be detected.
- Is it an alternative to GPS Map Camera or Timestamp Camera? Yes, for the same job, but free and open source with no ads, subscriptions or trackers, no Google Play services, an offline map, and signed photos.
- How do I add location and time to photos on Android? Install GeoTag Camera, allow camera and location, wait for "Location locked" and take the photo; the stamp is burned into the image and the location is also written to EXIF.
- Can I export photo locations? Yes: CSV (Excel, Google Sheets), KML (Google Earth) or GeoJSON (QGIS, ArcGIS), plus a PDF site report.
- Where do I get it? https://konkomaji.com/geotagcamera/download/ (signed APKs from GitHub releases).
